synchronization.strategy: merge only after final CI success, mergeable=true and behind_by=0; preserve unrelated concurrent work

implemented: explicit read-only Docker Engine backend attestation with fail-closed direct-socket override
fixed GET-only operation allowlist with no arbitrary API path method query or command
bounded daemon health and normalized container inventory
finite historical logs with tail since until byte item line and time bounds plus best-effort credential redaction
finite recent events with fixed object-type allowlist and minimized actor attributes
bounded image inventory with repository-reference caps and no labels or raw image configuration
bounded volume inventory without mountpoints labels driver options or warning payloads
bounded network inventory exposing aggregate attachment and IPAM counts rather than endpoint addresses MACs labels or options
single-container one-shot statistics using stream=false and one-shot=true with normalized CPU memory PID network and block-IO counters
aggregate resource inventory using exactly three bounded reads under one shared query budget without per-object inspect fan-out
aggregate-first diagnostic detail with deterministic anomaly selection before any detail request
diagnostic detail hard-capped to three candidates with request and fan-out budget preflight before backend work
multi-object diagnostic detail accepts no caller-selected container IDs and derives every detail target from the bounded aggregate inventory
dead and exited anomaly candidates remain visible as evidence but never trigger unreliable stopped-container stats calls
active selected candidates receive at most one non-streaming stats sample; automatic logs and events remain disabled
typed operation results with actor reason correlation ID and audit envelopes
documentation and deterministic tests for topology/secret minimization path validation finite diagnostics and load guards
security_boundary: production should use a least-privilege HTTPS authorization proxy because a read-only filesystem mount of the Docker socket remains protocol-privileged
no exec attach create start stop restart kill delete pull push build inspect fan-out or arbitrary Engine API operation
logs events and resource statistics never expose live streams
container log content remains potentially sensitive after best-effort redaction and is deliberately bounded
resource inventory omits volume mountpoints labels driver options network endpoint addressing and unbounded raw metadata
container stats require an exact validated container target and never return raw cgroup structures
aggregate-first detail derives exact stats targets only from normalized bounded inventory and skips stats for stopped candidates
writes remain absent; any future write layer requires a separate identity plus plan approval change verify idempotency pre-state rollback intent and independent readback
remaining: production authorization-proxy integration example with least-privilege endpoint policy
optional separately designed write layer only after the observe contract stabilizes
